title: What is your setup / workflow, and how do you ask AI to help you? (new to ai)
author: HeavyChance4249
selftext:
Curious how you are all setup with AI Coding / Asset creation / Game engine for your game project?

Like, what AI Agents are you using, what tier of subscription? What are you connections with software like, what Generators to help for assets, what are you asking AI to help you do with your project?  
Does it take an expensive subscription to build a game like the 100$/month?  
  
Do you just use the AI Agent to connect it to softwares like   
Claude > Blender MCP  
Claude > Unity3D MCP

;;;

I'm not a coder, I have basic Unity3D and C# beginner knowledge thats it lol

I recently got Claude Code Pro few weeks ago and have been learning there's many different ways to ask it to build something for you...  
  
  
like;  
"Build me a garbage collection system for the bullet projectiles"   
"I think I need a garbage collection system for my game, but I'm not a coder, guide me on what I should do"   
"when the bullets shoot out in my shooting game the screen gets really laggy and I'm not sure why how would you fix this problem?"  
  
Etcs lol

I wonder what other useful AI Agents or software there are for AI Gamedev...

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
$20 Anthropic sub

GitHub is my workhorse. First thing is repo setup, Issue/PR standards, linear atomic commits, CI, TDD protocol, etc.  Really lean hard on GitHub to keep the project on track.

For each new build I run a "grill me" style iterative design process to hammer out a spec.  Like about 50 PRs worth of spec work, usually using Sonnet.  That turns into a phased roadmap.  Each phase is composed of issues.

Then I use Opus 4.8 to build off the issues.  I target 500-1500 line diffs.  That seems to be the optimal size for Opus.  I'm balancing the capacity of the model with my capacity to keep track of what's being done.  Each phase includes a holistic QAQC/stitch pass and, more recently, a spec conformance review.

I have some routines set up to audit docs and create maintenance issues.  I was planning to set up routines for building but realized that I want to track progress it's easy enough to just prompt manually.  Sometimes I want to add a little steering clarification to the issue build prompt.

I do most of this from my phone.  Sometimes if it's going to be a long Q/A session I will open the laptop.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
I did use integrated AI, but found they got outdated too fast, so now I only use Browser AI.

My own questions are focused around making the AI predict the function.

    "Provide me with an simple Move() script. All it should do is make the Defualt Character controller of Unity move using WASD keys and the new Input System as the Input."
    
    "Using Cinemachine, and using the Player Input for the new input system. Create an script that allows me to rotate the camera around the player CameraRotation()."
    
    "Now that we have Movement and Camera, make the movement relative to the camera."
    
    "Not what I wanted. For movement instead I want the camera direction projected using ProjectOnPlane(). For now the Plane Normal is just Vector3.up. Respond by only giving me the Move() script."
    
    "Rotate the character controller, Look(), in the direction it is moving, smoothly. Rotating twice as fast when turning 180, but at normal rotation when turning 90, Use Angle() to compare."
    
    "Use character rotation and movement to play the Walking Animation Blend Tree, Animation()"

This is what it is like. Keep the task simple, and specify tools and functions you want. Keep it it's own little projects.

comments.body: I do vscode and codex plugin. It just cooks. You can connect to games engines and programs with the mcp server if it has one.

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body:
Codex with superpowers skill and Suno with a $200 subs each. 

A browser, VSCode, audacity, DaVinci  and Gimp

I had it look at my specs and install Comfy, a mesh generator, a song writer,  and other editing tools I've found in this sub to clean up art. I just need images not 3d assets, so I had Codex build a "workshop" studio that controls the integration of tools and asset management that gets promoted to production. After I ask Codex to make or move an asset I always follow up by asking it to make a manual control surface to launch and use the other AI tools.

There are plans and glossary of terms and it figures things out rather quickly. I don't often have to edit code directly but at the end of a "sprint" i will go in and fix colors, alignments, jewelry, fingers, etc and just add a human touch. Stuff where I have the skills and it's not annoying.

I then use the workshop to make assets and test them on a test server with my coworkers. Often they use similar tools to speed up generation and review. The review of assets takes the longest. But as the game gets flushed out I use less and less AI due to it making new tools.

I then switch to Suno and bash out music, then use minimax h3 to make a video using generated assets and add those assets. It ends with a press pack and everything the expansion needs and I send it to players.

I tweak things based on feedback. Often I have to regenerate from base files but it's easy due to having the pipeline.

replies.author: zayelion
replies.body:
You can find most of it here.

[https://universiatcg.com/press](https://universiatcg.com/press)

The problem with superpowers is that it creates an absurd number of tests, and you have to prune them from time to time, or else the time it takes to do anything grows and grows. But otherwise it forces the AI to behave like an ideal software developer that actually writes test first (in a decade I havent seen that in the wild). 

Minimax is installed locally, I have a week machine but its able to make an animation in an evening. My team also have it and can help out if need be, it takes them 10-30 mins each. Knowing general manipulation skills is also important.

While I cant say that the AIGen for everything is as good as things you will see here in this sub (Im blown away) we got from 0 to a steam demo in 3.5 months, and just crossed into month 4 doing polish with a release date in April. We already have players which is wild!
